subtitle: Monthly horror picks for the mortally curious.

novels.title: The Haar
novels.author: David Sodergren (2021)
novels.vibe: A folk-horror creature feature about an elderly woman defending her Scottish coastal home, wrapped in a rolling, unnatural sea fog.
novels.summary: Elderly Muriel refuses to sell her home in the fishing village of Witchaven to a developer's agents, and just as the pressure peaks, a strange fog — the haar — rolls in carrying something eel-like and hungry. The novel pairs a stubborn, sympathetic heroine with escalating, visceral creature-horror set pieces.
novels.warnings: Graphic sex scene, explicit language, self-harm and suicidal ideation (visceral depiction), body horror, gore, misogyny, violence.

novels.title: Home
novels.author: Ben Young (2024)
novels.vibe: A slow-burn small-town supernatural horror about a haunted house that's just been turned into the local funeral home.
novels.summary: In the dying town of Oak Hollow, Ohio, a long-notorious haunted house is converted into a funeral home just as the town's fortunes worsen. Told through alternating perspectives — a recluse, a grieving family, a hoarder, an abandoned child — the novel builds dread around grief and decay as much as anything overtly supernatural.
novels.warnings: Domestic violence, dementia, grief, psychological distress, references to child neglect.

novels.title: Bat Eater and Other Names for Cora Zeng
novels.author: Kylie Lee Baker (2025)
novels.vibe: A grief-soaked, gory mystery following a crime-scene cleaner who can't tell anymore what's real and what's the Hungry Ghost Festival catching up with her.
novels.summary: Cora Zeng cleans up after violent deaths in Chinatown for a living, still reeling from her sister's murder and the killer's parting slur: "bat eater." As she keeps finding dead bats at crime scenes tied to East Asian victims, and the Hungry Ghost Festival closes in, the line between anti-Asian violence, grief hallucination, and something genuinely supernatural blurs.
novels.warnings: Graphic violence and gore, anti-Asian racism/hate violence, animal death, death of a sibling, psychological distress.

novels.title: Suffer the Children
novels.author: Craig DiLouie (2014)
novels.vibe: Apocalyptic vampire-child horror that's really a gutting story about what parents will do for their kids.
novels.summary: A mysterious illness kills every child on Earth overnight — until they start coming back, animated and "alive" again as long as they're given blood. The novel follows several families forced to decide how far they'll go to keep their undead children fed, as society collapses around the impossible bargain.
novels.warnings: Child death, body horror, animal death (a pet), violence, themes of parental grief and moral compromise.

short_works.title: The Yellow Wallpaper
short_works.author: Charlotte Perkins Gilman (1892)
short_works.vibe: A claustrophobic feminist classic — a woman confined to a room for her "nerves" starts to see something moving in the wallpaper.
short_works.summary: Confined to a room and forbidden from working or writing by her physician husband as a cure for postpartum depression, a woman becomes fixated on the room's ugly yellow wallpaper. As her isolation drags on, she begins to see a figure trapped within its pattern, her grip on reality unraveling alongside her confinement.
short_works.warnings: Psychological horror, postpartum depression and mental illness, medical control/gaslighting, isolation.
